clue.text: After career, Wally and Elizabeth finding romance, perhaps?

indicators.note: the pieces that follow in the clue are placed after the word for career

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong, to tear along
a wally is British slang for a fool, a jerk
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone retires from a job and finds love with a fool called Wally and a woman named Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the fool and the queen come after the verb for career. A wally is British slang for a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental love story designed to make readers weep is a classic example of a weepie.

clue.text: As carrier, I dropped something hot in stumble

indicators.note: in says the exclamation and the letter for hot go inside the word for stumble

parts.note: to stumble is to trip
oops is what you say when you drop something
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and drops something hot while carrying it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel used to carry soldiers is a type of transport carrier.

clue.text: A northerner's cartwheeling shock

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cartwheeling turns the word over, so in this down clue it reads upwards

parts.note: a Lapp is a native of Lapland in the far north

explanation.surface: A northerner turning cartwheels causes a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay, giving someone a nasty shock.

clue.text: A basic requirement to pass is what's wanted

definitions.meaning: read literally, only the ticket is needed to get through a barrier
the idiom for exactly the right thing

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely what is needed, while a ticket is literally all that is needed to get past a barrier.

clue.text: With her standing to embrace clergyman, one's seemingly quite embarrassed

indicators.note: to embrace says the reversed word holds the other pieces inside
standing means upright, so in this down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written
DD, Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree
one is I and the apostrophe s is is, giving IS

explanation.surface: A woman stands to hug a vicar, who looks rather embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is only a link, and 'standing' works because in a down clue an upright word reads from the bottom; the definition describes a face that looks slightly flushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat red in the face looks like a blush, so a person appears a little embarrassed.

clue.text: Case that used to be more than big enough?

parts.note: ex means former, what something used to be
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A suitcase that once was roomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is an instance or illustration.

clue.text: Give out? It's supposed to be money back!

indicators.note: back tells us the word for what is supposedly money is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the proverb says time is money

explanation.surface: A complaint that a payout should have been a refund of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the saying 'time is money'; 'back' turns that word around.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out a sound, light or smell is to discharge or send it forth.

clue.text: Pig's breakfast Cain and I prepared with great passion

parts.note: a pig's breakfast is British slang for a mess

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, worked up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A messy meal that Cain and I cooked up with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pig's breakfast' is British slang for a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Messianic zeal is fervent, evangelical enthusiasm, the passion of a would-be saviour.

clue.text: Seek out suspicion

definitions.meaning: a slight hint or suggestion, as a suspicion of garlic

explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to track down, and a trace of something is a faint hint of it.

clue.text: Hostile to work set

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
to set a question is to pose it, so set can mean posed

explanation.surface: Someone resents being given a piece of work to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something means standing in opposition, unfriendly to it.

clue.text: US city, impressive American capital

parts.note: august describes something majestic, inspiring awe

indicators.note: capital means the initial or capital letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A description of a grand American state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like part of the definition (Augusta is the capital of Maine) but it picks the first letter of 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is a city in Georgia and also the state capital of Maine.

clue.text: PM greeting more ridiculous Nigerian leader loves to punch the thug

indicators.note: to punch means to break into, so these pieces go inside the word for thug

parts.note: a goon is a thug
dafter means sillier, more ridiculous

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Nigerian

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so loves gives two Os

explanation.surface: A ridiculous Nigerian leader greets the Prime Minister with a punch at a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like Prime Minister but means post meridiem, the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: PM is the time after midday, and this is the salutation used then.

clue.text: One up, or one in bed

indicators.note: in says the letter for one goes inside the word for bed

parts.note: a flower bed is a plot of ground
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A choice between someone who is awake and someone still lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One up' describes someone up in the air, flying a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The person flying an aircraft is up aloft, so an airborne flyer is one up.

clue.text: Make do when the devil is in range

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: in says the word is goes inside the verb for range

parts.note: to range is to wander or rove
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to makeshift measures when the devil comes within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with whatever is to hand, extemporising.

clue.text: This for the luck of the draw?

definitions.text: This for the luck of the draw?

parts.words: This for the luck of the draw?
parts.note: a horseshoe is hung up for luck, and a magnet draws metal; the phrase 'luck of the draw' fuses the two

explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped magnet looks like a lucky horseshoe and attracts, or draws, iron objects.

clue.text: Make a chiming sound faintly resonate

definitions.meaning: to seem vaguely familiar, to stir a dim memory

explanation.definitionFit: To ring a bell literally sounds a chime, and figuratively means to seem vaguely familiar.

clue.text: So locked in combat here, forever

indicators.note: locked in says the answer is held inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Two combatants are locked together in battle, here for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: So, as a conjunction, means for that reason, consequently.

clue.text: Under one's nose, a hairline fracture has come up with client

indicators.note: to fracture is to break, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient arrives with a hairline crack in a bone just below the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairline fracture' reads as a medical phrase; 'hairline' belongs to the definition and 'fracture' is the anagram signal for HASCOMEUP plus CLIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin, neatly trimmed line of whiskers growing on the upper lip, just below the nose.

clue.text: Repairman covers a circuitous route

indicators.note: covers says the repairman word goes around the letter

parts.note: a mender is someone who repairs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A repairman takes a roundabout way to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A winding, wandering path is like the looping course of a river.

clue.text: Put down what's been picked up: new grass in pot

definitions.text: Put down what's been picked up

indicators.note: in says the new grass goes inside the word for pot

parts.note: an urn is a pot or vase
a lea is grassland, a meadow

explanation.surface: A gardener sets down a pot after planting new grass in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' means learned, not lifted, and 'Put down' means discard.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlearn is to discard knowledge or habits one has acquired.

clue.text: Reject left during second dance

indicators.note: during says the letter for left sits within the word for second

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone is turned down for the second dance and left out.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote against admitting someone to a club, traditionally with a black ball, is to reject them.

clue.text: County for young men

definitions.meaning: short for Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London

explanation.definitionFit: Buckinghamshire is an English county, and a buck is a lively young man.

clue.text: Search is widespread — criminal finally caught

indicators.note: caught says the widespread word holds a letter within it

parts.note: something rife is widespread

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of criminal

explanation.surface: A large-scale search ends with the offender caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a drawer is to ransack or search it hurriedly.

clue.text: Hot lover?

parts.note: a ... is hot, and a sweetheart is an old ...

explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is called a flame, and a fire is literally hot.

clue.text: Had cold, then placed by the fire?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
something placed by the fire is warmed, heated

explanation.surface: Someone who had a cold was sat beside the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' is the slang sense of conned, not the past of have.
explanation.definitionFit: To be had is to be fooled or swindled, so had means swindled.

clue.text: One's stoned, a detailed outspoken affair

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, the final letter removed

parts.note: someone outspoken is vocal
a do is a party or social affair

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs has a frank, much-discussed affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' suggests drugs but means having a stone, as this fruit does.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped fruit has a single large stone at its centre.

clue.text: Fish that's under a foot?

definitions.meaning: a flatfish such as the Dover variety
the underside of a foot or shoe

explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish shares its name with the underside of the foot, which it resembles in shape.

clue.text: Relative ending race out of sorts

indicators.note: out of sorts means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner finishes a race feeling unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's granddaughter is a family relation.
